turns.final_message:
This repo already has the fix, so I didn't change any code. Your running app is almost certainly loading an older copy of flask_admin.

Your traceback has `field.entries,` at line 100 of `validators.py`. That's the old `ItemsRequired`, which assumed every field was an inline form with `.entries`. The code here at `flask_admin/contrib/sqla/validators.py:103` reads `.entries` only when the field has it. Otherwise it counts `field.data`, so multi-select fields like `QuerySelectMultipleField` don't crash. Its docstring dates this change to 2.2.2.

I tested it from this repo:
- A multi-select field with items passes.
- An empty one gets the normal "At least 1 item is required" form error instead of crashing.

flask_admin isn't installed anywhere I can see outside this folder, so I couldn't find which copy your app uses. On your side:

1. Run `python -c "import flask_admin; print(flask_admin.__file__)"` in the environment that runs the admin.

3. Restart the server.

One snag: `pyproject.toml` still says `version = "2.2.1"`, but the code already has the 2.2.2 fix. Pinning `flask-admin==2.2.1` from PyPI will give you the old, crashing code, so install from this repo.

If it still crashes after that, send me the new traceback and the path from step 1.
